nodes.text: Which calibration? Forecasting and judgment (do your 70% calls come true about 70% of the time), ML model calibration (do predicted probabilities match observed frequencies), measuring instruments, or something else?
What is 'the stuff we talked about'? That earlier conversation isn't available here, and there are no notes in the workspace. Paste or summarise the points you want to cover.
What is the one claim the piece should leave readers with? That becomes the thesis.
Who reads the newsletter, and what do they already know about calibration? That decides whether the piece starts by defining it or skips ahead to the argument.
What evidence do you have: your own track record, a dataset, a study, an anecdote? Every claim needs an evidence slot, and none can be filled yet.
Length and register: a short note or a long essay? Is there a practical takeaway (a habit, a check, a tool)?
